newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 20.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
- U.S. President Bill Clinton's Administration has reduced to 800 from 4,000 the number of soldiers it will send to Rwanda.
- New York's Court of Appeals has ruled that people can seek monetary compensation from the state government for violating their rights under the state constitution.
- The Central Intelligence Agency suspects the officer that it arrested for giving secrets to Russian intelligence gave a lot more information than it had anticipated.
- The State Department and seven major U.S. airlines have agreed to notify the families of victims of future air disasters abroad much quicker than they have in the past.
- The U.S. government will pay $4.8 million as compensation for having injected 12 people with radioactive plutonium or uranium in secret experiments during the cold war.
- The U.S. vote against a second term for Boutros Boutros-Ghali as secretary general of the United Nations has set the stage for a prolonged battle over the future of his career.
- The former Texaco Inc executive who divulged recordings of other executives talking horribly about black employees has been charged with obstructing justice.
